label: Storage Orchestration Pro
summary: Advanced storage lifecycle orchestration covering performance/resilience tiers, pools, volumes, measured capacity, encryption-key references, snapshots, replication and controlled migration across qualified local or distributed providers. Each engine's durability, consistency, effective quota and restore semantics remain explicit.
core_boundary: Core retains essential local storage/device policy, filesystem quotas, ownership, encryption boundaries, ordinary snapshots where admitted and local backup/restore. This module adds advanced cross-pool/provider policy and orchestration; native storage/provider foundations remain open source, and no package receives arbitrary device paths, raw mount commands or the only recovery key.
acceptance: Qualify each engine/version/topology and storage tier using observed latency, resilience and durability characteristics; a tier name never proves performance or redundancy.
Resolve authoritative pool/volume identities, tenants, capacity, inode/IO limits and mounted workload dependencies before allocating, moving, expanding or retiring storage.
Review encryption-at-rest support, key references, rotation, escrow/recovery and failure behavior without exporting plaintext keys into package data or logs.
Coordinate snapshots with application/database consistency and retention; a local snapshot is not evidence of an independent backup or a tested restore.
Qualify replication direction, lag, snapshot compatibility, fencing and recovery-point selection before an orchestrated promotion or migration.
Exercise full pools, read-only filesystems, interrupted copies, failed mounts, concurrent changes and lost connectivity with explicit uncertain outcomes and reconciliation.
Refuse destructive pool/volume/snapshot actions without current authority, resource revisions, dependency review and an independently verified recovery reference.
Removing or expiring orchestration must preserve mounted workloads, Core storage control, retained snapshots/backups, key recovery and a supported service-specific exit route.
